angle: What was announced and what was not

sources.title: Cloudflare acquires Deno to improve its Workers programming model

claims.claim: TechCrunch published a piece headlined: Cloudflare acquires Deno to improve its Workers programming model
claims.evidence: Cloudflare will use this acquisition to improve its Workers programming model and platform.

claims.claim: Cloudflare announced on Friday that it is acquiring Deno, the startup behind the programming runtime of the same name.
claims.evidence: TechCrunch: Cloudflare announced Friday that it's acquiring Deno.

claims.claim: Cloudflare's Kenton Varda, principal engineer for Workers, said the acquisition will be used to improve the Workers programming model and platform, on which customers build and run software on Cloudflare's network.
Deno was co-founded by Bert Belder and Node.js creator Ryan Dahl.
Deno recently launched celld, an open source implementation of Workers.
claims.evidence: TechCrunch: recently launched celld, an open source implementation of Workers.

claims.claim: Varda rejected the theory that Workers was made different from other cloud platforms to create lock-in.
claims.quote: being open source and giving people an escape hatch is good business

claims.claim: Ryan Dahl said his team is joining Cloudflare to make the Workers programming model mainstream.
claims.quote: joining Cloudflare to make the Workers programming model a mainstream way to build servers

claims.claim: Financial terms were not disclosed; Deno had raised $26 million in total, including a Series A led by Sequoia.
claims.evidence: TechCrunch: terms not disclosed; raised a total of $26 million.
